svg.text: REPORT 2 · FRAME 2 OF 4
AGENTIC BLUEPRINT
How the system is put together: who does the work, what stops a mistake, and where the real work goes.
Benchmarked against the Claude Code standard — agents with narrow tools, checks that run automatically, decisions written down.

g.text: 11 of the fourteen agents have done real work; 3 are waiting for a phase that has not happened
How many times each agent was handed a task, counted from the session logs. 55 dispatches to these fourteen; 10 more went to general-purpose helpers that sit outside the roster.
3 of 14 have never been dispatched: diagram-cartographer, evidence-clerk, handoff-scribe.
That is not idleness. Each belongs to a phase of the design process this project has not reached yet — there is no user research to log, and nothing has shipped to hand over.
Six ways to stop a mistake, ranked by how hard they are to ignore
The rule of the system: never solve with a written rule what a permission can solve.
Strongest at the top. Prose is the weakest layer, which is why only two rules live there.
The agent is never given the tool
The save is refused before it happens
The build goes red after the fact
Someone can see it went wrong
A rule in prose, and nothing more
Every layer names a real file. A layer that named nothing would read as coverage while protecting nothing — which is the exact failure this list was built to prevent.
What the agents actually spent their time doing
The twelve most-used tools, counted from the session logs.
2,574 tool calls in total across 5,904 agent turns.

svg.text: What this means
11 of fourteen agents have done real work. The 3 idle ones
map to phases this project has not reached.
Every enforcement layer names a real file. The weakest layer,
prose, carries only two rules on purpose.
The busiest tools are reading and running things — the agents
spend most of their effort checking, not writing.
No agent holds a Figma tool. This board was written by the
main session, because the grant was never made.
What to do next
Make the ADR-007 Figma grant now that a real file exists, and
test it rather than assume it.
Give the 3 unused agents their first real task, or retire
them from the roster.
Keep the routing table as the single place that decides who
does what — it already routed 55 dispatches to the roster.
Add a counter for the autonomy ladder, which is still
declared but not operative.

CoForge · measured from the git history and the session logs, frozen at 2026-09-08 12:11 UTC (the last record in the corpus, not the time the script ran) · every transcript record counted once, keyed on message uuid · dollars are illustrative at Opus 5 list price and were never billed
The repository counts do not include this report: it was committed after the figures were frozen, so the artifact and commit totals here are one behind by construction.
